description_en: The Vīranārāyaṇa temple is a dedicatory temple commissioned by the 11th Prime Minister Bir Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana. The Temple is situated at the central courtyard in the inner sanctum of the Tīnadhārā Pākaśālā, a residential building built by the same prime minister to provide accommodation for the students of Sanskrit. At present, the location of the Pākaśālā is at Durbar Marg, Kathmandu. Although established in reverence and worship of Lord Vishnu, the temple, however, as suggested by the prefix ‘Vīra’ is taken after the patron of the temple, Bir Shumsher. This tradition of naming temples after the patron or in memoria of family and friends is unique to Nepal, and the case of Vīranārāyaṇa temple is simply a continuation of that tradition. The earliest known example of this kind of dedicatory temple in Kathmandu valley is that of Bhimbhaktesvara temple established by Bhimsen Thapa.The general established the temple in his own name (Bhim) as a devotee (bhakta) of Lord Siva. Example dedicatory temples also exist from the time of Rana and Shah rulers. (Add more examples of such dedicatory temples with footnote citation later)Of the legion of temple architecture found in Nepal, the oldest, and what is often described as characteristically niche to Nepal, is acknowledged as the pagoda style- a tiered tower with multiple eaves common to Hindu temples in East Asian countries. Changu Narayan, Nepal’s oldest known temple is a two-tiered pagoda tower. In Nepal, the temple construction takes the form of identity markers. Each ruling dynasty of Nepal has introduced a distinctive temple structure that has become associated with their name. Temple construction as an ambitious undertaking is understood to have mnemonic function used by the patrons to forge associations of the king and the deity, in praise and devotion of the deity for the support of his rulership, in public memory.  Among the noted and distinguished temple tops, beyond the times of the Malla kings, there are three that are more prominent than the others: dome, bell and lotus shaped tops.This departure from the favoured architectural design of the pagoda style of the Mallas was not given continuum by the new generation of rulers. Perhaps, to distinguish themselves from their predecessor and to commence their own reign with a mark of devotion as represented in their distinct temple style architecture, the new class of rulers, the Ranas, Kunwars, Pandes and Thapa initiated new temple building activities in Kathmandu. The bell-shaped top originates from Gorkha, the capital of the Shah kings. The largest assemblage of consecutive bell-shaped top temples can be found high above the river in Deopatan, where elven temples are built in a row on a terrace high above the river which were established within only six years, between 1858 and 1864, in close similarity to one another. But, perhaps the most elaborate is the Hridayaesvara temple at Cupinghat in Bhaktapur.The introduction of dome-top temple architecture in the Kathmandu Valley marks a significant evolution in Nepalese religious structures, largely credited to Prime Minister Bhimsen Thapa, who served as the de facto ruler in the early 19th century. The pioneering example of this architectural style is the Bhimbhaktesvara Temple, built in 1822 by General Bhimsen Thapa himself, and named in his honour. Nestled within the lush grounds of his garden, the Janarala Bag, this temple showcases a traditional design characterised by a square sanctum and an inner ambulatory. Elevated on a triple-stepped platform, the temple's core rises prominently to support a distinctive bulging dome, a feature that symbolises the fusion of local and foreign influences in architectural design. The construction of the Bhimbhaktesvara Temple reflects the introduction of building traditions from Lucknow, India. Its exterior is adorned with a white plastered surface, fluted pilasters, and an array of Anglo-Indian decorative motifs, including the acanthus leaf, which had been embraced in the region long before, tracing back two millennia to the northern plains of the Indus.The most elaborate, in design and engineering, is the construction of lotus-shaped top as observed in the Vīranārāyaṇa temple. The white plastered temple has a lotus shaped dome top with unfurling petals gradually opening as it descends to the flower base from the golden shrine/ Gajur atop. The body of the temple has windows facing the four cardinal directions, decorated in Mughal style arched windows. It also has neoclassical pilasters framing the temple structure that has an octagonal foundation. The most innovative element of this temple is the introduction of a dome on pendentives. Beginning with the Bhimbhaktesvara temple of 1822, all of the domes were characterised by a pseudo-vault constructed from corbelled bricks, necessitating a supporting timber framework. The Vīranārāyaṇa temple is guarded by Lord Vishnu’s mount the Garuda, which is situated on top of a tall tower, whose back bears untranslated inscription. Newer additions in the form of temples of gods and goddesses of the Hindu pantheon around the temple complex.The ruling dynasty of Nepal before the Ranas had associated architecture styles that became symbolic of their reign. As rulers of the Himalayan Kingdom where the architectural aesthetics and principles derived from the Newars, the architecture style the Ranas would promote would have to reflect their desire to be outwardly as well as be emblematic of their rule. The resulting conflation of these two interests are well reflected in the diverse temple architecture styles built during their time. These temples, however, are also testament to the far reaching influence of the Rana kings which often materialised in the knowledge and skills they imported from their neighbouring state kingdoms like Lucknow which manifested in the architecture. The frequent visits to the Princely states of India by the Rana prime ministers could be accounted for the awe and amazement at the architectural landscape and the subsequent inspiration for the incorporation of those foreign motifs into the Hindu temple architecture could perhaps explain the emergence of a distinct style introduced during their 104 years rule. Many scholars on the subject hypothesise that the artisans and craftsmen were brought over from India to provide adequate training to transfer skills to emulate the style of Indian architecture and engineering mechanism. The use of white plaster on temple walls and on residential palaces, dome top, Mughal style windows are a result of those acquired skills that proliferated and dominated the building history of the Ranas.Understanding the Guthi system is essential for appreciating the cultural fabric of Nepal, which is defined by a collective commitment to preserving its heritage. Guthi is a social system of the Newar people in Nepal that supports the socio-economic status of their community. Guthi includes trusts to which lands are donated, a deed considered worthy of religious merit, which are used to generate revenue. These revenues are allocated for various projects including restoration of temples, patis (rest houses), maths (priest houses) and Hitis or Dhunge dhara. A Guthi is established with the purpose of looking after the cultural heritage of the community past their construction.The Guthi established by Bhīma Śamśera for Tīnadhārā Pākaśālā and Vīranārāyaṇa manages the property and the encapsulated temple. While the exact date of the construction is yet to be determined, it can be cautiously concluded that the temple was built well before the first known directive sent out by the Guthi in 1945 VS, which details account of deposition made by a patron named Jujuvīra before the Guthi Administration Office regarding the operations of two specific Guthi organisations: Tīnadhārā Pāthaśālā Guṭhī and Vīranārāyaṇa Guṭhī. Regular contributions to the Guthi allowed for the management of the two properties over the years. This inference is well supported by the earliest instructions from the royal authority commanding overseeing various tasks for the welfare of the two guthis. Prime Minister Bir Shumsher established the Tīnadhārā Pākaśālā to provide residential service for the learners of Sanskrit. Prime Minister Bir Shumher was a known orthodox Hindu (as noted in the book Ranas of Nepal) whose motivation to promote the learning of Sanskrit language can be understood from the role priests played as community leaders leading not only religious practices and sharing old knowledge, but also serving as an ideal model who teaches, gives advice and sets a good example for others to follow. Priests are revered members of the community whose councils are sought by Kings and Prime Ministers at their court. As a gesture of respect, meals in the royal household were only taken after the bell in the pakashala rang, notifying the royal palace of the completion of meals taken by the priest, informs Niraula, a resident administrator at the pakashala. His orthodox Hindu background could help us understand his initial intention behind the establishment, however, his dedication to oversee the welfare of the institution can be discerned from the various legal orders and documents issued by the prime minister to manage the place through Guthis. For instance, a document from 1947 VS documents the assigning of a sum of 88 rupees and 14 ānnā to conduct daily rituals of the deities. There are also executive orders signed by the prime minister providing funds for feeding 108 Brahmins of Tīnadhārā Pāthaśālā (VS 1947), as there are documents instructing the whitewashing of the building of the pākaśālā. The pakashala was a well administered institution whose matters of daily functioning were meticulously recorded. Guthi as a social system and institution is a great initiative from community members that acknowledges the role of tangible heritage in community making, and therefore involves the community in ensuring the longevity of its tangible cultural heritage.The Vīranārāyaṇa temple is an integral part of the community at Teendhara pakashala, where it serves not only as an important deity of worship for its members, but also as a representation of the continuing belief in the importance of Sanskrit in training students in the ancient language for courtly and religious administration. The Kalmochana guthi, the guardian body of the temple, oversees the functioning and well-being of the temple, executing its operations. A designated priest, appointed and salaried by the guthi, is responsible for the worship in the temple that takes place in the morning and evening. The guthi generates its income in the same manner as it has since its inception, through revenue earned from the proceeds of cultivated land leased to farmers in whose name the land has been registered. It functions independently of the government and has its own representative office to which taxes are paid.The pakashala accommodates 111 Sanskrit scholars selected through a competitive entrance exam administered by its patron institution, the Nepal Sanskrit Vishwavidhyalaya. Traditionally, only students from the three Brahmanical castes - Upadhyaya, Acharya, and Shastri - could be admitted into the pakashala and pathashala. However, in the Sanskrit lexicon, these three castes do not strictly correspond to modern-day castes; rather, they represent academic statuses pertaining to the level of education achieved by a tutor. Upadhyaya loosely corresponds to a teacher of Sanskrit grammar who has completed the equivalent of modern-day undergraduate studies. Acharya signifies a teacher who teaches and leads by example, while Shastri in Sanskrit means a scholar who has complete knowledge of the Shastras. These educational titles, while connotative of the calibre of the teacher, became social products of inheritance and were passed down hereditarily to future generations, transforming into social castes from statuses and solidifying as such in public memory. Nevertheless, after democracy became the form of government, a legal court verdict issued in 1958 AD mandated the admission of students enthusiastic about Sanskrit, irrespective of their caste in the Hindu caste system.The Garuda, a mythical bird and the mount of Lord Vishnu, holds a prominent place in Hindu mythology. Known for his immense strength and speed, Garuda is often depicted as a half-man, half-bird figure, symbolizing the union of the spiritual and physical realms. His association with Vishnu underscores the deity's role as the preserver of the universe, with Garuda serving as his loyal companion and protector. The Garuda's presence atop the Vīranārāyaṇa Temple not only enhances the temple's architectural grandeur but also signifies the divine protection and guidance bestowed upon the devotees who gather to worship within its sacred confines.
description_ne: नेपालको ११ औं राणा प्रधानमन्त्री वीर शमशेरद्वारा काठमाडौंमा संस्कृत अध्ययनरत विद्यार्थीका खातिरखान-बस्नपाकशालाकोनिर्माण गरेका थिए । उक्तपाकशालासंगैयो मन्दिर तिनै प्रधानमन्त्रीद्वारा निर्माण भएकाले यसलाई‘वीरनारायणमन्दिर’ भनिएको हो ।काठमाडौंकोतीनधारामाप्रधानमन्त्री वीरशमशेरलेसंस्कृत पढ्ने बटुक ब्राह्मणकाखातिरपाकशालाकोनिर्माण गरेका थिए । उक्तपाकशालामाचारैतिर आवासीय भवन बनाई बीचमा ठुलो चोक निकालिएको छ । सोही चोकको केन्द्रमावीरनारायणमन्दिर अवस्थित छ । वीर शमशेरले बनाएको कृति भएकाले उनैको नाम उतारी‘वीरनारायण’भनिएको हो । नेपालमा चारैतिर संरचना बनाई बीचमा चतुष्कोणाकार चोक बनाउने थिति निकै पुरानो हो । उपत्यकाका सबैनेवाःबस्तीमाबाहाः,बही, चुक,ननिजस्ता चोकको प्रधानता छ । यस्ता चोकको बीचमा मन्दिर वा चैत्य बनेकासयौँउदाहरण पाइन्छन् ।पाकशालाकोचोकमा पनि यही मान्यताबाट प्रेरित भई नारायणको मन्दिर उठाइएको छ । पूर्वाभिमुख मन्दिर पाँच तहको पेटीमाथि उठाइएको छ । मन्दिरको पेटी र गारोअष्टकोणाकारमाछ । यहाँको पेटीमा अब्बल जातको कालो ढुङ्गा र स्तरीय कालिगढी देख्न सकिन्छ । मन्दिरमा आठवटा कोणमा गोलाकार खम्बा उठाइएका छन् । माथिल्लो भाग दुई तह कमलको पत्र आकारमा बनाइएको छ । फूलमाथिको भाग गुम्बज वा घण्टशैली भन्दाअलि पृथक छ ।गजुरचढाउनउँचोभागमा कोण पार्दै लगी अन्तमागजुरहालिएको छ । मन्दिरका चौतर्फी काँठका चौकोस रखापा युक्तढोकाहरू हालिएका छन् ।ढोका माथिकोभागमासुर्कीकोप्रयोगबाट मुगल शैलीको अर्धगोलाकार बुट्टा प्रयोगमा छ । गर्भगृहमा विष्णु र उनका साथमा सरस्वती र लक्ष्मी उभिएको धातुको मूर्ति छ । मन्दिर अगाडि नारायणका वाहन गरुडको स्तम्भ खडा गरी मूर्ति हालिएको छ । पेटी बाहिर फलामेरेलिङ्गमापित्तलका पालाहरू लहरै राखिएका छन् । नेपालमावेल्डिङ्गप्रविधि भित्रनु पूर्वको यस फलामेरेलिङ्गरोचक छ । राणाकालमा पुल, ढोका, बत्तीका खम्बा, ढलको ढकनी आदिमा नयाँ तवरले ढालिएका फलामे सामग्री(cast-iron)प्रयोगमा आउन थालेको थियो । यहाँ दियोको खातिर उठाइएकोरेलिङ्गपनि यसै दौरान प्रयोगमा ल्याइएको नयाँ प्रविधि थियो । मन्दिर आसपास शिवलिङ्ग एवं अन्य देवदेवीका मूर्तिहरू थपिएका छन् । मन्दिरको बाह्यभागमा बज्रको लेप लगाई सेतो रङ्ग पोटिएको छ । नेपाली निर्माण जगतमा बज्रको लेप र सेतो भित्ताको प्रयोग भीमसेनथापाको समयदेखि भएको हो । भीमसेन थापाको प्रसिद्ध वाग दरबारको अगाडि राजपुत शैलीमा दुई ठुला मन्दिर बनेका थिए । तीमध्ये एक भीमभक्तेश्वर मन्दिर (KAT0700) हो जुन नेपालमै नौलो वास्तु स्वरूपको मन्दिर थियो (Gutschow 2011, p. 874) । यस मन्दिर बनेपश्चात् नौलो वास्तुलाई अंगाल्दै १९ औं शदीमा क्रमशः अन्य मन्दिरहरू बन्दै गएको पाउँछौं जसमध्ये यो मन्दिर पनि पर्दछ । यूरोपेली, मुगल, राजपूत र नेवार वास्तुशैली पनि प्रयोग भएकाले यसलाई कतिपय विद्वानहरूले हाइब्रिड अर्थात् मिश्रित शैली पनि भनेका छन् । पाकशालस्थित यो मन्दिरसंग मेल खाने दर्जनौं मन्दिरहरू वागमती किनारका घाटमा पाइन्छन् । जङ्गबहादुरद्वारा निर्मित कालमोचन मन्दिरको चौतर्फी भएका गुम्बज मन्दिरसंग यसको वास्तुस्वरूप हदैसम्म मेल खान्छ ।पाकशालाभित्र विसं १९८२ (सन् १९२५) मा राखिएको वृहत ताम्रपत्र छ । उक्त ताम्रपत्र अभिलेखमा विसं १९४३ वैशाख शुदी तृतीयादेखि शासकबाट गुठी प्रणालीको व्यवस्था भएको कुरा उल्लेख छ । यसै उल्लेखनलाई आधार मानी हाल प्रशासनलेपाकशालाकोशुभारम्भ मिति मान्ने गरेको छ । अभिलेखमापाकशालासंगैमन्दिर बने-नबनेको कुरा स्पष्ट खुल्दैन । तर पाकशाला संगसंगै वीरनारायणका नामले मन्दिर पनि उठाइएको अनुमान सहजै गर्न सकिन्छ । विसं १९४५ (सन् १८८८) को गुठी सम्बन्धि लिखित सामग्रीमापाकशालासंगैयस मन्दिरको पनि प्रसंग परेकाले दुबै संरचना एकैसाथ निर्माण भएको कुरालाई थप बल मिल्दछ (K_0037_0019F) । राणाकालीन विविध लिखित सामग्रीहरूमावीरनारायणर यसको गुठीका प्रसंग परेका छन् । विसं २०४७ (सन् १९९०) सालमा तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री कृष्णप्रसाद भट्टराईको उपस्थितिमापाकशालाकोसतवार्षिकी मनाइएको थियो ।निर्माणकालदेखि प्रयाप्त आय व्यवस्था सहित गुठी प्रणालीबाट चल्दै आएको यस मन्दिरको पूजा परम्परा आजभोलि (सेप्टेम्बर २०२४) नियमित रूपमा हुन छाडेको छ । राणाकालीन गुठीका लिखतहरूबाट यहाँ वर्षवर्धन र विविध पर्वपूजा पनि हुने गरेको तथ्य खुल्दछ जुन लोप भैसकेका छन् । जानकारहरूका अनुसार हरिबोधनी एकादशीका दिन विगत विशेष पूजा गरी प्रसाद बाँढ्ने चलन थियो (one of the staffs of the Pākaśālā, male, age ५४) ।

historical_events.event_description: पाकशालाभित्र विसं १९८२ (सन् १९२५) मा राखिएको वृहत ताम्रपत्र अभिलेख छ । उक्त अभिलेखमा विसं १९४३ वैशाख शुदी तृतीयादेखि शासकबाट गुठी प्रणालीको व्यवस्था भएको कुरा उल्लेख छ । यसै उल्लेखनलाई आधार मानी हाल प्रशासनले पाकशालाको शुभारम्भ मिति मान्ने गरेको छ । अभिलेखमा पाकशालासंगै मन्दिर बने-नबनेको कुरा स्पष्ट खुल्दैन । तर पाकशाला संगसंगै वीरनारायणका नामले मन्दिर पनि उठाइएको अनुमान सहजै गर्न सकिन्छ । विसं १९४५ (सन् १८८८) को गुठी सम्बन्धि लिखित सामग्रीमा पाकशालासंगै यस मन्दिरको पनि प्रसंग परेकाले दुबै एकैसाथ निर्माण भएको कुरालाई थप बल मिल्दछ (K_0037_0019F) ।
वीर शम्शेरका नाममा स्थापना भएको वीरनारायण मन्दिरमा उनकी कान्छी महारानीबाट एक घण्ट चढाइयो ।

पाकशाला र वीरनारायण मन्दिरको वार्षिक कार्यका खातिर आय र खर्च व्यवस्थाको विस्तृत ताम्रपत्र अभिलेख लेखी पाकशालामा टाँसियो । यो अभिलेखीकरण कार्य श्री पूर्वतर्फका कमाण्डर जनरल धर्म शमशेर राणाका मर्जी मार्फत् नारामान भक्तले गरेका हुन् ।
वीर शम्शेरका नाममा स्थापना भएको वीरनारायण मन्दिरमा उनकी कान्छी महारानीबाट विसं १९४४ (सन् १८८७) चढाइएको घण्ट बिग्रेकाले जीर्णोद्धार गरियो ।
विसं २०४७ (सन् १९९०) सालमा तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री कृष्णप्रसाद भट्टराईबाट यस पाकशालाको सतवार्षिकी मनाइएको थियो ।
